runs.text: When I was twelve, my stepfather killed himself in front of my mother. I was giving my four-year-old sister a bath. I didn’t see the act, but I saw the aftermath, the blood- and brain-soaked walls, the chaos. I was the one who ran barefoot down the street to the neighbor’s house to call 911 with my sister wrapped in a towel. No adult was able or willing to do it. I went back to call my stepdad’s family to tell them what happened.

Three days before, my abuser, a man from my mom’s past, had paid a visit to our family home. After the suicide, he stayed. CPS got involved. My mother didn’t admit the truth or try to protect me. Instead, she told them I was out of control. She lied to avoid giving up my abuser. That’s how I ended up in the system.

Thirteen placements in three years. Every home was for “high-risk” kids. The abuse didn’t stop; it just changed form. Staff members crossed lines. Some just looked away. I learned quickly: manipulation was survival. If I wanted anything, it was safety, comfort, a moment of fucking peace. I had to perform, predict, outmaneuver. “Seeking” stopped meaning hope; it meant strategy. Don’t expect a story about innocence here. This is about what you become when every door is closed except the ones you learn to pry open.
This is how I knew it was over,
and you didn’t even bother with clearing it.
to a better version of us

pieces.title: The Day I Married the Wind

runs.text: I wore sneakers and a velvet jacket.
carried six birds and a scent I couldn’t place.
We exchanged vows in a parking lot.
He never liked being told where to go.
I never liked being left with doorframes swinging.
He never confused silence with love.
He just circled the house three times,
kissed every loose page off my desk,
And every time a gust kicks up,
I check the air for his fingerprints.
I never asked to see this much.
Never asked to feel people’s truth
I used to call it crazy.
God didn’t give me visions to hoard.
He gave me the fire to carry.
And sometimes that fire burns me first.
and choosing to still love them.
in a world that calls it hysteria.
I am the prophet with the scarred throat.
and learning to wait for the feedback.
Half a blowjob for an hour of sleep.
Your name for a new one
This is kill or be killed.
so he could skip the small talk.
